html:
Coca is a shrub of the eastern slopes of the Andes whose leaves have been chewed or brewed as tea for thousands of years. It eases hunger, cold and altitude sickness, and is sacred in Andean religion.

Under the Inca Empire coca was used in rituals and by the elite. After the conquest, the Spanish sold it in huge amounts to the miners of Potosí. It is grown in the Yungas valleys near La Paz and in the Chapare. In the 1800s chemists isolated cocaine from it.

From the 1970s the cocaine trade to the United States made coca a source of money, violence and US pressure. Coca growers' unions of the Chapare, led by Evo Morales, fought eradication. Bolivia defends chewing the leaf as a tradition, while the same crop fuels the conflict in Colombia.
